mstts:express-as.prosody:
Welcome to a journey where roots sink deep into the earth, branches stretch for the sky, and together, we search for meaning in all the spaces in between.
Through the words and reflections found in Tree of Life with Spiritual Poetry by Nataša Pantović, we’re invited to explore self-discovery in a way that blends mindfulness with the gentle beauty of poetic insight.
Just imagine—every living thing is connected, forming a tapestry that’s always growing, changing, and renewing itself. Isn’t it amazing how the cycles of nature can mirror our own transformations?
As you listen, you’ll notice spiritual poetry flowing through each moment, giving us a peek into the mysteries of existence and revealing the subtle wonder tucked into everyday life.
As the seasons shift and the tree’s shape changes, we’re invited to see how our own understanding of consciousness and presence can grow. Each poem, each meditation, is like a stepping stone—helping us gently explore our inner world with curiosity and openness.
The wisdom of nature, the rhythm of your own breath, and the quiet power of really noticing what’s around you all come together here, guiding us toward a deeper sense of harmony and purpose.
So, as we begin, let’s open our hearts to the wonders this journey holds. Together, we’ll discover how mindfulness, poetry, and the lessons of nature can inspire us to embrace life’s unfolding beauty.

Chapter 1: Discovering the Web of Life—How Everything Connects
Have you ever had one of those rare, quiet moments—maybe right after a rainstorm or early in the morning—when the world suddenly feels both endless and incredibly close?
In that hush, it’s almost like the lines between you and everything around you start to blur.
That’s where this journey begins.
Imagine a tree: every branch, every leaf, each root—each part is unique, but together, they create one living, breathing being.
That image sets the stage for what we’re about to explore—the deep, often hidden connections that link all life.
Picture someone sitting beneath a huge, old tree. They lean back, feeling the rough bark against their skin.
All around, life keeps moving—cars rush by, people hurry past. But under that canopy, time seems to slow. Sunlight filters down in shifting patterns, and for a moment, the tree isn’t just part of the scenery; it’s an active participant in the moment.
Its roots stretch deep, drawing strength from the same earth that supports all living things. The air drifts between the tree and the person, connecting them with every breath.
When you pause long enough to notice, it’s clear—nothing exists in isolation.
Most of us rush through our days, pulled in a million directions, barely noticing these subtle connections.
But when we slow down and really pay attention, the links between everything become obvious. The tree’s leaves flutter thanks to sunlight and rain—gifts from above. The soil, full of fallen leaves and tiny creatures, feeds the roots. Even a little ant, hurrying along a branch, plays its part in this living network.
What if you could see yourself as part of this web?
It’s not just about appreciating nature’s beauty. It’s about realizing that every action, every thought, every feeling, sends ripples outward.
A kind word, a moment of patience, even a silent hope—they all reach further than you might ever know.
The tree, standing tall through wind and sun and changing seasons, becomes a quiet teacher. Its ability to adapt, endure, and grow offers us lessons on how to face life’s ups and downs.
There’s a story that comes to mind—someone feeling lost and disconnected, who starts spending time in a local park. At first, it’s just a quick walk, maybe a short sit on a bench.
But over time, they notice the small things: trees changing with the seasons, birds returning in spring, fresh leaves unfolding. Slowly, a sense of belonging grows. The park stops being just an escape, and becomes a gentle reminder that connection is always possible, even during tough times.
This sense of unity isn’t only about nature—it also reaches into our relationships, our communities, and even the world inside our minds and hearts.
What if, instead of focusing on what separates us, we looked for what brings us together? Every encounter, every conversation, becomes a chance to connect and heal.
And throughout this journey, poetry weaves in and out, like a bridge between thought and feeling. Each poem is like a leaf—unique, but part of something bigger.
So, here’s the key takeaway: life is a tapestry of relationships, and every one of us, every being, has a place woven into it.

Chapter 2: Mindful Presence — Finding Stillness in Everyday Life.
You know, with all the noise and demands of modern life, this idea of mindfulness can feel almost out of reach. But here's the thing—mindful awareness isn't about escaping reality. It's about really showing up for every single moment, no matter how ordinary it might seem.
Picture this: someone stands at the kitchen sink, hands deep in warm water after a long, hectic day. Deadlines, distractions—they've all piled up. But as those dishes are washed, something shifts. The focus moves from swirling thoughts to the gentle feel of water, the sound of porcelain, the fresh scent of soap. For just a few breaths, the world shrinks down to this one simple act. And suddenly, there's a sense of calm. It's almost as if peace finds you—not because anything outside has changed, but because you've changed how you meet this moment.
Most of us slip into autopilot. We race from one task to the next, barely noticing the richness of our own experience. But this chapter invites you to pause, even if just for a heartbeat, and really pay attention. Mindfulness isn't about strict rules or doing it perfectly. It's more like a gentle reminder—coming back to the present, again and again. Maybe it's noticing the sunlight spilling across your table, hearing laughter drift in from another room, or just feeling your own breath as it comes and goes.
There's a story in the book about a parent overwhelmed by the beautiful chaos of family life. Mornings are wild—lunches to pack, shoes to find, arguments to settle. But one day, right in the middle of all that, the parent pauses to watch their child tie their shoes. Small fingers fumble, a tongue pokes out in determination. And for just that moment, everything else fades away. The parent doesn't just see a task—they see a child learning, growing, becoming. And suddenly, frustration melts into gratitude.
The book makes it clear—mindfulness isn't about getting it right every time. Distractions will happen, emotions will bubble up, and your mind will wander off. But that's okay. The practice is to notice, to gently return, and to start over, as many times as you need. Over time, this kindness toward yourself opens up space for new insights and a softer, more compassionate way of being. The inner critic starts to let go, and acceptance quietly grows in its place.
Poetry weaves its way throughout this chapter, acting as a gentle guide. These verses invite you to slow down, to savor the tiny, beautiful moments, and to really listen to the rhythms of life all around you. Through poetry, even the most ordinary things become sacred, and the present moment turns into a kind of refuge.
And mindful presence isn't just for peaceful, quiet times. You can bring it into your conversations, your work, even when things get tense. By listening with your whole heart, speaking kindly, and pausing before you react, your relationships can shift in powerful ways. The book reminds us—mindfulness isn’t just a practice, it’s a way of being. It's a path that leads you inward, to the quiet stillness that’s always there at the heart of your life.

Let’s wander into Chapter 3: Nature’s Lessons—Wisdom from the Living World.
Imagine stepping outside, breathing in the fresh air, and realizing the world around you is bursting with hidden wisdom. Nature isn’t just a pretty backdrop—it’s like a gentle, patient teacher, quietly offering guidance if you’re willing to listen.
Think about it—every tree, every river, even the smallest stone has a story to tell. Stories about bouncing back, about embracing change, and about the never-ending cycles of life.
Picture someone strolling through a forest right after a heavy rain. The ground is soft beneath their feet, and the air is thick with the scent of earth. Puddles mirror the sky above, while birds sing from hidden branches. Suddenly, they spot a fallen tree, its trunk blanketed in moss and tiny mushrooms. At first, it feels a little sad—something once strong has fallen. But look closer, and you’ll see life everywhere. Insects are busy, new plants are starting to grow, and all that decay is feeding the soil. What looked like an ending? It’s really just another beginning.
Nature gently reminds us that nothing stays the same forever. Seasons change, storms pass, and life keeps moving. Here’s something to pay attention to: endings aren’t failures—they’re just part of a bigger cycle. When trees let go of their leaves each autumn, they make room for fresh growth in the spring. If we hold on too tightly to old habits, or clutch painful memories, we might be missing the chance for something new and beautiful to bloom.
There’s a story here about someone going through a tough transition—maybe it’s losing a job, moving to a new place, or the end of a relationship. At first, it feels overwhelming, like being completely uprooted. But spending time in nature, watching how plants adapt and animals find new ways forward, brings comfort. Slowly, trust grows—a belief that, even in uncertainty, something good can emerge.
Nature also teaches us patience. Seeds can sleep underground for months before they finally sprout. Rivers shape entire canyons, but it takes centuries. Personal growth? It’s often a slow process—slower than we’d like. If you rush it, frustration creeps in. But if you trust life’s rhythm, peace follows.
The poetry in this chapter draws inspiration from sunrise, gentle rain, and the quiet strength of roots beneath the ground. Each poem invites you to look closer, to listen a bit deeper, and to discover wisdom in the everyday moments. Nature becomes a mirror, reflecting both your strengths and your vulnerabilities. When you pay attention, you learn how to weather storms, celebrate new growth, and find rest in stillness.
Here’s an invitation: spend time outdoors, move slowly, and notice the little details you’d usually miss. As you do, you’ll rediscover that sense of wonder. The world starts to feel like a place full of surprises, and every day brings a new lesson to learn.

Chapter Four: The Journey Inward—Growing Through Spiritual Practice.
You know, the search for meaning often draws us inward, into those quiet corners of the heart and mind where real transformation can begin. Spiritual growth isn’t just a goal you check off a list—it’s a journey. And it’s a path that unfolds with curiosity, humility, and a real openness to change.
What’s powerful is that this journey looks different for each of us. It’s shaped by our own stories, beliefs, and that deep longing for something more.
Picture this: someone sits alone in a small room, a single candle flickering on the table. After a long, noisy day full of demands, there’s finally a moment to just be still. Their eyes close, and the only thing to focus on is the gentle rhythm of their breath.
Thoughts wander in and out—worries, hopes, little memories. But slowly, a sense of spaciousness grows inside. In that quiet, something shifts. The lines between “me” and “the rest of the world” start to blur, replaced by a gentle feeling of connection.
Spiritual practice can take so many forms—maybe it’s prayer, meditation, quiet reflection, or simply small acts of kindness. The truth is, the exact form doesn’t matter nearly as much as the intention behind it. What really counts is showing up, being present, and listening with your whole heart. Over time, these small moments become a way of coming home to yourself, a way of remembering what truly matters.
There’s a story about someone who’s constantly battling self-doubt. The inner critic is loud—always pointing out every flaw and mistake. But through gentle spiritual practice, they learn to greet those thoughts with compassion. Instead of pushing them away or arguing, they get curious: “Where did these ideas come from? Are they even true?” Slowly, the grip of self-judgment begins to loosen, and a real sense of acceptance starts to grow.
Of course, the journey inward isn’t always smooth. Old wounds can resurface, and sometimes the path feels lonely. But here’s something important: struggle is part of the process. Growth often means facing what’s uncomfortable, sitting with it instead of running away. In those moments, turning to poetry or wisdom from others can offer real comfort—a gentle reminder that you’re not the only one walking this path.
Gratitude weaves through this whole journey. The invitation is simple: notice the gifts that are already here. Maybe it’s a friend’s kindness, a moment of beauty, or just the miracle of being alive. Practicing gratitude shifts our focus from what’s missing to what’s abundant, opening the heart to unexpected joy.
In the end, spiritual growth is about becoming more fully yourself—not about being perfect, but about embracing your strengths and your flaws. The journey keeps unfolding, day after day, with no finish line in sight. And every single day brings a new chance to learn, to grow, and to connect just a little more deeply with the world around you.

Chapter 5: Poetry as a Path to Wholeness
Poetry moves through this book like a gentle current, quietly inviting you to dive a little deeper into your own reflections and discoveries. It’s more than just words—these verses are little invitations to pause, to really listen, and to feel what’s stirring inside you. Poetry becomes almost sacred here, a way to gently touch what’s most real and true about who we are.
Picture this: it’s late at night, the house is silent, and someone is reading a poem under the soft glow of a lamp. The words echo in the quiet, reaching into the depths of the heart. There’s something comforting about realizing we’re not alone—others have felt the same longings, the same doubts, the same hopes. In those moments, a poem becomes a companion, maybe even a guide through the winding paths of our own soul.
When it comes to writing poetry, the book invites you to see it as an act of presence. It’s all about slowing down, paying attention, and letting your emotions bubble to the surface. You don’t need to write for anyone else—just for yourself, as a way to explore your inner life. Forget about perfect lines or clever rhymes; what really matters is honesty. It’s about being willing to open up, to put your feelings into words, no matter how raw or messy they might be.
There’s a story in here about someone who starts a journal during a tough time. At the beginning, their entries are scattered—just lists of worries, fragments of memories, even questions with no answers. But slowly, the writing takes on a rhythm. Patterns start to appear, insights bubble up, and the simple act of writing becomes a kind of healing. The journal turns into a safe place—a spot to untangle confusion and celebrate the little victories along the way.
Poetry also has this amazing way of connecting us. Sharing a poem, or just reading one together, can build a bridge between people. It’s like getting a glimpse into someone else’s world. The book reminds us that poetry is the language of the heart—something that goes beyond our differences and brings us together. In a world that can feel divided, that sense of shared humanity is such a gift.
The poems in this book draw from nature, moments of stillness, and the search for meaning. Each one is an invitation to slow down, to take a breath, and really listen. Through poetry, the ordinary moments of life start to feel extraordinary, and suddenly, the journey toward wholeness is lit up in new ways.
Before wrapping up, the book leaves us with this gentle reminder: poetry isn’t just for poets. Anyone can find meaning in a well-chosen word, a remembered line, or a quiet moment of reflection. Poetry is a path—a way to come home to yourself, to spot beauty even in the struggles, and to celebrate the mystery of being alive.

Chapter 6: The Heart of Compassion — Opening to Others.
Have you ever noticed how the world can feel heavy sometimes? Maybe it’s the news, the struggles of someone you care about, or just that quiet ache of loneliness that sneaks in now and then. In moments like these, compassion isn’t some far-off ideal—it’s a force you can actually feel, something that softens even the toughest days. Compassion, at its heart, is just what happens when we allow ourselves to stay open.
Imagine this: a neighbor walks home, glances over, and sees an elderly person wrestling with their groceries. There’s that split second—do they stop and offer to help, or just keep moving? If they choose to reach out, maybe with a smile or a steadying hand, something shifts. Both people walk away changed. The one who helps feels a spark of purpose, and the one who’s helped feels noticed, maybe a little lighter.
Most of us don’t realize just how much these little moments matter. You might think compassion needs to be some huge gesture, but honestly, it’s found in the simple things. Like listening without judging, offering an encouraging word, or just being there when someone’s hurting. These small acts? They ripple out, often way further than we see.
There’s one story that really sticks with me—a teacher notices a student pulling back. Grades are dropping, laughter's fading. Instead of scolding, the teacher chooses to sit with the student at lunch. No lecture. Just quiet company and a shared sandwich. Over time, trust starts to grow, and the student opens up. The burden they’ve been carrying gets a little lighter. It’s a powerful reminder: compassion isn’t about fixing people. It’s about walking beside them, even when things are hard.
The poetry in this chapter is so gentle—filled with images of hands reaching out, hearts opening, burdens shared. Each verse is a quiet nudge, reminding us that everyone’s carrying something invisible, and that kindness is never, ever wasted.
And you know what? It’s not just about how we treat others. The book encourages us to practice compassion for ourselves, too. That’s actually the foundation for loving others well. We so often fall into the habit of criticizing ourselves, thinking if we’re just a little tougher, we’ll finally improve. But what if, instead, we tried some gentleness? When we meet our own mistakes with understanding—not blame—our hearts start to soften. That’s when real healing can begin.
Compassion is a practice. It’s a way of being in the world that grows stronger the more you lean into it. It’s not always easy—sometimes it means sitting with discomfort, or facing where we fall short. But every act of kindness, no matter how small, brings us closer to a world that’s more connected, more loving, and a little bit lighter for everyone.

Chapter 7: Gratitude’s Quiet Power—Transforming the Ordinary
You know, gratitude doesn’t always make a grand entrance. Most days, it slips in softly—like sunlight drifting through your window first thing in the morning.
When life feels overwhelming or just plain routine, it’s so easy to miss those little moments. But here’s the beautiful thing—the real magic of gratitude is that it can quietly change how you see even the most ordinary days.
Picture this: someone wakes up before dawn. The house is still, shadows everywhere, and they’re carrying a heaviness—maybe it’s worry about work, or just a lingering sadness that won’t quite leave.
And yet, as they move through their morning, something simple happens. They feel the warmth of a mug in their hands. They notice the sky turning from gray to gold. And just for a moment, gratitude flickers.
It’s not about pretending the pain isn’t there. It’s about letting yourself notice what’s good, even when things are tough.
There’s a story in the book about someone starting a gratitude journal. At first, it’s all pretty basic—writing down a good meal, a kind word, maybe a favorite song. But after a while, it starts to change them. Suddenly, gratitude isn’t just a list—it becomes a new way of seeing.
They begin to spot beauty in the small things—a stranger’s smile, a flower pushing through a crack in the sidewalk, the comfort of their daily routine. And little by little, the world feels lighter, somehow more alive.
Most of us wait for big moments to feel grateful—a job promotion, a vacation, some big milestone. But what if gratitude isn’t really about those things? What if it’s about the everyday gifts we usually pass by?
When you start to notice the small mercies—the quiet moments that get you through the day—gratitude becomes a balancing act. It doesn’t mean hardship disappears, but it reminds you that joy and sorrow often show up together.
There’s this memory of a family gathered around a table, sharing stories and laughter. The meal is simple, but the feeling of belonging fills the room. In that moment, gratitude isn’t just an emotion—it’s a way of being. You realize it’s less about what you have, and more about how you see what’s right in front of you.
The poetry in this chapter is gentle, filled with images of light, warmth, and the quiet abundance of everyday life. Each poem feels like an invitation—pause for a second, take a breath, and give thanks.
The book encourages making gratitude a daily habit—not because you have to, but because it’s a gift you give yourself.
So, what’s the real power of gratitude? It’s a doorway to joy. It opens your heart, makes pain a little softer, and pulls you right into the present moment.
In a world that loves to point out what’s missing, choosing gratitude is actually a radical act of hope.

Chapter 8: Embracing Change — The Art of Letting Go
Change is always with us. Sometimes, it drifts in quietly, like a gentle breeze. Other times, it sweeps through our lives like a storm, shaking everything up. Let’s take a closer look at the art of letting go, and why it can feel both painful and strangely freeing.
Letting go isn’t about giving up. Instead, it’s about making space—space for something new to enter your life.
Picture this: someone is packing up their childhood home. Every object they touch—a faded photograph, a battered old toy, a letter tucked away in a drawer—holds a memory. There’s a tug of sadness, a real fear of losing what once was. But as those boxes fill and the rooms start to empty, something shifts. The memories don’t disappear, even though the space is changing. Suddenly, it’s clear: when we hold on too tightly, we can get stuck. But when we let go, life has room to move forward.
Most of us resist change at first. We cling to familiar routines, old relationships, or even the identities we’ve built over the years. It’s totally normal to feel afraid—to grieve what’s being left behind. But here’s something to pay attention to: every ending can hide a new beginning. Think about trees in autumn. They let go of their leaves, and in doing so, they make way for fresh growth in the spring.
There’s a story here of someone facing the end of a friendship. That loss hurts—it leaves a real emptiness. At first, it’s tempting to distract yourself or even turn bitter. But as time passes, there’s an opportunity to sit with the pain, honor what was, and trust that something new will eventually take shape. It’s slow, but healing has its own pace.
The poetry woven through this chapter is bittersweet. There are images of leaves drifting down, empty nests waiting in quiet trees, and wide open skies. Each verse is a gentle nudge, reminding us that change is woven into the rhythm of life. Letting go isn’t weakness—it’s an act of courage.
So, trust the process. Even when it feels like you’re facing a loss, remember that renewal is possible—sometimes in ways you can’t imagine yet.
Here’s the thing: letting go isn’t a one-time decision. It’s a practice. It takes patience, a little self-kindness, and a lot of faith that life will unfold as it should. When we choose to embrace change, we become more resilient, more open, and somehow, more fully alive.

Chapter 9: The Soul’s Unfolding—Living with Purpose.
There comes a moment when our search for meaning shifts. Suddenly, it’s not just about asking “why am I here?” but “how can I live in a way that really matters?” This chapter invites us to think about what it truly means to align our lives with the deepest longings of the soul.
Here’s the thing—purpose isn’t a finish line you cross. It’s more like a way of moving through the world, guided by intention and integrity.
Picture someone standing at a crossroads, feeling the weight of choosing the “right” path. It’s easy to get stuck in the fear of making a mistake. But, what if purpose isn’t about making one perfect decision? What if it’s about listening—really listening—to that quiet voice inside, to the needs around us, and to the opportunities that show up in everyday life?
Let me share a simple story. Imagine a person stuck in a job that’s lost its spark. Every day feels the same, and restlessness starts to creep in. Then, one afternoon, they decide to volunteer at a community garden, helping kids plant seeds. The work is humble, but something inside shifts. Suddenly, there’s a sense of being alive, connected, and truly useful. And in that moment, it becomes clear—purpose isn’t about status or big achievements. It’s about service, creativity, and genuine connection.
A lot of us grow up thinking that purpose has to be grand or world-changing. But this book gently pushes back, showing us that meaning often lives in the ordinary moments. Purpose can be as simple as raising a child, tending a garden, making art, or just being there to listen. What really matters is the intention behind what we do.
The poetry woven throughout this section is bright with hope. You’ll find images of seeds sprouting, new paths unfolding, and hearts waking up. Each poem is an invitation: trust the journey, follow what brings you joy, and let your sense of purpose reveal itself over time.
Living with purpose, the book reminds us, means becoming more fully yourself. It’s about letting your actions line up with your values, listening to your intuition, and having the courage to take some risks along the way. Be patient with yourself. Trust that your path will become clearer, step by step. And remember—every single life has value.
Purpose isn’t something you have to find. It’s something you live—one day, one choice, one small act of kindness at a time.

Let’s take a gentle walk into Chapter 10: Returning to the Tree—Wholeness and Belonging.
As we wrap up this journey, we find ourselves once again under the branches of the tree.
Think about it—the tree’s always been there, a symbol of wholeness, resilience, and belonging. Its roots dive deep into the earth, while its branches stretch bravely toward the sky. Leaves shimmer and whisper in the light. It’s weathered storms, let go of leaves, and welcomed new ones. But through it all, the tree stands strong—a living reminder that life moves in cycles, and we’re all part of that rhythm.
Picture this: someone sitting quietly beneath a tree at sunset. The air’s cool, everything feels still. Maybe it’s been a long day—full of both laughter and a few tears. As the sun dips below the horizon, there’s this gentle peace that settles in. Suddenly, they feel connected—to the tree, to the earth, to the people they hold dear, and even to something bigger than themselves.
Here’s something to really pay attention to: wholeness isn’t about being perfect. It’s about welcoming every part of ourselves—the bright spots and the shadows, our strengths and even our tender vulnerabilities. Belonging, it turns out, isn’t about squeezing ourselves into a mold—it’s about showing up as we truly are. Just like the tree, with its unique twists and scars, our own stories make us beautiful.
There’s a lovely story here about a community planting trees in a barren field. At first, it’s tough work, and change comes slowly. But over time, those trees start to grow. They offer shade, shelter, and a sense of beauty. That empty field transforms into a place where people gather—a symbol of hope and renewal. And it becomes clear—belonging isn’t something that just happens. It’s built, little by little, through shared effort, care, and genuine love.
The poetry in this final chapter glows with images—roots wrapping around each other, branches reaching out, sunlight dancing through leaves. Every verse feels like a celebration of how deeply we’re all connected. It’s a gentle reminder: even when we feel alone, we’re part of something much bigger.
So, as the book closes, there’s this quiet invitation: bring the lessons of the tree into your own life. Root yourself in what truly matters. Reach for the light. And whenever you can, offer shelter to someone else. Because wholeness and belonging aren’t places we arrive at—they’re ways of living, nurtured through everyday attention, a little compassion, and a whole lot of gratitude.

As we wrap up this journey, here’s an invitation for you: let the wisdom of the tree truly take root in your everyday life. All those ideas—connection, mindfulness, nature’s lessons, spiritual practice, poetry, compassion, gratitude, embracing change, having purpose, and feeling like you belong—they aren’t just things to check off. They’re meant to become part of how you live and breathe. Think about it: every small act of kindness you offer sends ripples out into the world, often in ways you’ll never even see. When you’re present and mindful, even the most ordinary moments can fill you with peace and meaning. Nature’s cycles are always reminding us—change and renewal are not just possible, they’re part of being alive.
When you meet life with gratitude and compassion, your heart opens to joy, even when things get tough. And living with purpose? It’s not about chasing grand achievements. It’s about showing up with intention, right where you are.
You don’t have to have it all figured out, or walk this path perfectly. Think about a tree—it grows slowly, weathers storms, and soaks up sunlight, always reaching for what it needs. Just like that, you get to grow at your own pace. Rest when you need to. And trust that you belong, exactly as you are.
So, let the poetry of your life unfold, one breath, one step, one day at a time. If you ever feel lost, come back to the tree—whether it’s a memory, a real tree in nature, or that quiet place inside your heart. There, you’ll find the strength to start again, the courage to let go, and the joy of knowing you’re part of something so much bigger.
The journey continues, and you’re never truly alone.
